title:
Vacuum handling device having a suction nozzle
and gripper part contained within a single housing

features.item: A housing with a grip portion designed as a hollow body for gripping
features.note: The reference describes a housing unit that is a hollow body, but it does not explicitly mention a 'grip portion' designed as such for gripping.

features.item: An electrically operated vacuum generating device in the housing
features.note: The reference describes a vacuum source operating on an ejector principle, which typically uses compressed air, not an electrically operated device.

features.item: Exhaust air from the vacuum generating device guided through the hollow grip portion to an air outlet
features.note: The reference does not describe exhaust air being guided through a 'hollow grip portion' as the vacuum source is ejector-based and the housing is a hollow body, but not specifically a grip portion for exhaust.

features.item: A sound-damping device arranged in the grip portion
features.note: The reference does not mention any sound-damping device or a grip portion.

features.item: A suction plate comprising a carrier plate and a seal fastened to the carrier plate extending around it
features.quote: The gripper part 26 has, at its free end axially opposite to the housing unit 4, a flexible suction cup 27 or an at least partially flexible suction plate, which is secured in a sealing manner to a plunger body
features.note: The reference describes a flexible suction cup or suction plate secured in a sealing manner to a plunger body, which acts as a carrier. However, it does not explicitly state the suction plate comprises a separate carrier plate and a seal fastened around it, but rather a flexible suction plate secured to a plunger body.

features.item: A grip unit with hollow grip portion, electrically operated vacuum generator, exhaust air routed through grip to outlet, and sound-damping device in grip
features.note: The reference does not describe a grip unit with these specific combined features, particularly an electrically operated vacuum generator or sound-damping device.

features.item: Vacuum handling apparatus with suction plate and grip unit combined
features.quote: A vacuum handling device comprises includes a vacuum source having a suction nozzle means ( 6 ) operating on the ejector principle and furthermore a suction gripper ( 3 ) which possesses a gripper part ( 26 ) connected with
features.note: The reference describes a vacuum handling device that combines a vacuum source and a suction gripper with a gripper part (suction plate equivalent) in a single housing unit.
features.refuted: The quote describes a suction gripper with a gripper part, but does not establish that a suction plate and grip unit are combined in the claimed manner.

features.item: Grip portion at least partially lined with sound-damping material
features.note: The reference does not mention a grip portion or sound-damping material.

features.item: Vacuum generating device arranged completely in a first housing portion
features.quote: The vacuum source 2 comprises a suction nozzle means 6 with one or more suction nozzles. In the working example of FIG. 1 a single suction nozzle 7 is provided.
features.note: The reference describes the vacuum source being part of the housing unit, but it does not explicitly define a 'first housing portion' where it is completely arranged.

features.item: Sound-reducing device in the first housing portion or first housing portion lined with sound-reducing material
features.note: The reference does not mention any sound-reducing device or material in any part of the housing.

features.item: Grip portion elongated between first and second housing portions with air outlet on second housing portion
features.note: The reference describes an elongated housing unit and an air outlet, but not a 'grip portion' elongated between defined first and second housing portions with an air outlet on the second portion.

features.item: Air collection screw upstream of grip portion in first housing portion for collecting exhaust air
features.note: The reference does not describe an air collection screw or a grip portion.

features.item: Bent or curved air baffles downstream of grip portion directing exhaust air to air outlet
features.quote: Following this the pressure medium is directed by a deflector wall 24 of the suction nozzle 7 to the laterally arranged outlet 17 .
features.note: The reference mentions a deflector wall directing pressure medium to an outlet, which functions similarly to a baffle. However, it is not explicitly downstream of a 'grip portion' and is within the suction nozzle itself.

features.item: Battery coupling point on second housing portion with air baffles directing exhaust air away from battery coupling point
features.note: The reference does not describe a battery coupling point or air baffles directing exhaust air away from it, as the vacuum source is ejector-based.

features.item: Grip unit and suction plate releasably connected via a coupling device
features.note: The reference describes the vacuum source and suction gripper as a rigid structural unit within a housing unit, not releasably connected.

features.item: Grip unit with suction opening fluidically connected to suction chamber delimited by suction plate
features.quote: The gripper part 26 has an aspiration duct 42 extending axially through it. Such duct opens at one end into the active plenum 35 and at the other end into a suction space 43 delimited by the Suction cup 27
features.note: The reference describes a gripper part with an aspiration duct connecting to a suction space delimited by a suction cup (equivalent to a suction plate). However, it does not explicitly define a 'grip unit' with a suction opening in the same way the feature is phrased.

claims.quote: The invention relates to a vacuum handling device comprising a vacuum source, which possesses a suction nozzle means adapted to operate on the ejector principle and furthermore a suction gripper which possesses a gripper part connected with the suction side
claims.note: The reference discloses a vacuum handling device with a vacuum source and a suction gripper, which could be considered a grip unit. However, it does not specify it for a 'hand-operated laying device' or 'for use with a suction plate' as a primary component, though a suction cup is mentioned.

claims.quote: The vacuum handling device 1 is composed of two principal parts, that is to say a first part in the form of a vacuum source 2 and a second part in the form of a suction gripper 3 . These
claims.note: The reference discloses a housing containing a vacuum source and a suction gripper. It does not explicitly mention a 'grip portion for gripping the grip unit' or an 'electrically operated' vacuum generating device, as the vacuum source operates on the ejector principle using a pressure medium.

claims.quote: Preferably the housing unit 4 is designed in the form of a hollow body, which contains a cavity 5 which is preferably continuous in the longitudinal direction and in which the principal components of the device are accommodated.
claims.note: The reference states the housing unit is preferably a hollow body. However, it does not specifically state that a 'grip portion' (which is not explicitly defined) is designed as a hollow body.

claims.quote: Finally the suction nozzle 7 furthermore possesses an outlet opening 16 which is connected with an outlet 17 opening to the outer face of the housing unit 4 , and accordingly leading into the atmosphere, from the housing unit 4
claims.note: The reference describes exhaust air being discharged from the housing unit to the atmosphere. However, it does not state that this exhaust air is guided 'through the grip portion' (as a distinct element) or that a 'sound-damping device is arranged in the grip portion'.
This reference does not disclose a sound-damping device arranged in the grip portion.
This reference does not disclose a grip portion at least partially lined with a sound-damping material.
This reference does not disclose a vacuum generating device arranged completely in a first housing portion of the housing.
This reference does not disclose a sound-reducing device arranged in the first housing portion or the first housing portion being lined with sound-reducing material.

The reference describes a housing unit with a vacuum source and a suction gripper, but does not distinguish between a first and second housing portion with an air outlet arranged on the second housing portion.
The reference does not disclose an air collection device, such as an air collection screw, arranged upstream of the grip portion for collecting exhaust air.
The reference does not describe bent or curved air baffles arranged downstream of the grip portion for guiding exhaust air to an air outlet.

The reference does not disclose a battery coupling point for an electrical energy storage device or rechargeable battery on the housing, nor air baffles for directing exhaust air away from such a point.
The reference does not mention air baffles for directing exhaust air away from a battery coupling point.

claims.quote: A vacuum handling device comprises includes a vacuum source having a suction nozzle means ( 6 ) operating on the ejector principle and furthermore a suction gripper ( 3 ) which possesses a gripper part ( 26 ) connected with
claims.note: The abstract describes a vacuum handling device.

claims.quote: The gripper part 26 has, at its free end axially opposite to the housing unit 4 , a flexible suction cup 27 or an at least partially flexible suction plate, which is secured in a sealing manner to a plunger
claims.note: The reference discloses a suction plate or suction cup secured to a plunger body, which can be considered a carrier plate, and mentions it is secured in a sealing manner, implying a seal. However, it does not explicitly state the seal extends around the carrier plate.
The claim refers to 'said grip unit according to claim 1', but claim 1 of the subject invention is not provided, making it impossible to assess this limitation.
The reference describes a gripper part with a suction cup, but does not mention a releasable connection between a grip unit and a suction plate via a coupling device.

claims.quote: The gripper part 26 has an aspiration duct 42 extending axially through it. Such duct opens at one end into the active plenum 35 and at the other end into a suction space 43 delimited by the Suction cup 27
claims.note: The quote describes an aspiration duct within the gripper part that connects to a suction space (suction chamber) delimited by a suction cup (suction plate) to generate vacuum for holding an object.
claims.refuted: The assertion describes a 'grip unit' with a 'suction opening' connected to a 'suction chamber' to generate a vacuum between a 'suction plate' and an object.
